manuscript_policy.limitations_4_1: 'uncertainty weighting was enabled in the DP sweep experiments (privacy_utility_curves.py) but not in the base architecture experiments (run_exp1.py), which used equal task weights. This difference is a potential confound ...'

report.base_experiment_weighting: uncertainty (Kendall et al. 2018) for VFL-MTL; single-task baselines: n/a (one active task)
report.whether_comparison_is_confounded: Not by task weighting: base (run_exp1) and DP sweep (privacy_utility_curves) both used uncertainty weighting. They did differ in patience (15 vs 0) and seed sets, which are the actual confounds (both fixed: T10 patience 15 everywhere; revision sweep runs both on seeds 7,42,123,0-6). The manuscript's claim of equal weights (Eq. 3) and its §4.1 description of the confound are both inconsistent with the code that produced the results.

evidence.method: Uncertainty-weighted runs log the learned per-task sigma (train.py: row['sigma_{task}'] only when uncertainty_weighting is on). Fraction of rows with sigma_* filled in the published result CSVs:
evidence.results/privacy_utility_combined.csv: 1.0 at every epsilon and mode (learned sigma_ihm ~0.894, sigma_decomp ~1.083, sigma_pheno ~0.891)
evidence.results/ablations.csv: UNKNOWN - CSV has no sigma_* columns; code configured uncertainty weighting for the VFL-MTL reference
code_before_fix: experiments/run_exp2.py: True for all_tasks and ihm_decomp, False for ihm_only and ihm_pheno
experiments/run_factorial_pcmu.py: True when more than one task is active

decision.chosen: A - equal weights everywhere; Eq. 3 kept as written
decision.decided_by: author (2026-10-17), re-confirmed after the evidence above
rationale: All experiments are rerun anyway (alignment fix, T16), so A and B cost the same.
Fixed weights keep the privacy-utility analysis clean: learned weights shift with DP noise, mixing the noise effect with re-weighting (R1-Q4).
Matches the method the manuscript already describes (Eq. 3).
The effect of weighting stays measured: the revision sweep keeps uncertainty weighting as a labelled side arm at epsilon = inf and 5.
decision.supervisor_note: Inform supervisor: published multi-task runs used uncertainty weighting; corrected runs standardise on equal weights per Eq. 3, uncertainty kept as a side experiment.

after_fix.verification: configs import with equal weights only; synthetic sweep: equal arm logs no learned sigma, uncertainty arm does; pytest + regression check pass; no files written outside smoke_tests/

manuscript_updates_for_T17: Keep Eq. 3 (now true for all reported runs).
Rewrite the §4.1 weighting sentence: the confound it describes did not exist as stated; corrected runs use equal weights throughout.
Response letter: disclose that the original multi-task results used uncertainty weighting contrary to Eq. 3, and that all results were rerun with equal weights.
